title: Incident operator coaching and stakeholder communication framework
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Summary:
This document describes a coach-first approach to on-call and incident response at Redwood Inference. It combines a lightweight, prescriptive incident lifecycle with an operator mentorship program and standardized stakeholder communication templates. The goal is to 1) reduce time-to-stable, 2) make incident learning explicit, and 3) ensure consistent, brand-safe customer messages for incidents involving inference, KV cache, and control-plane services.

Scope:
- Services in scope: inference-gateway, router-scheduler, kv-cache, console-api, metrics-collector.
- Audience: responder engineers, bridge operators, support lead, CSMs, engineering managers.

Principles (why this differs):
- Coach-first: every new on-call pairing is a 1:1 coach shift for the first 2 weeks rather than unsupervised solo duty.
- Scripted communications: status/CSR language is templated to reduce risk of incorrect claims or legal exposure.
- Lightweight evidence capture: minimum artifacts required for postmortem and regulatory evidence.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Primary Responder: owns initial triage for 0–30 minutes, runs containment steps. (Typical role: on-call engineer)
- Coach (paired for new responders): shadow for the first 60–90 minutes, then provide guidance and ownership handback. Responsible for mentoring and incident evidence review.
- Bridge Operator: runs the incident bridge, maintains incident timeline, publishes status updates.
- Incident Lead: takes over restoration and remediation decisions if incident escalates past 90 minutes or impacts SLOs.
- Support/CSM Liaison: prepares customer notices and compiles account impact lists.

Incident lifecycle (Coach-first):
1) Alert & acknowledge (0–5m)
   - Primary responder acknowledges pager in PagerDuty within 3 minutes for SEV2+.
   - Create an incident in the bridge tool (bridge.redwood.internal/new) using the template "coach-first-bridge".
2) Rapid triage & containment (5–30m)
   - Identify affected service(s), region(s), and customer tiers: run CLI commands: 
     - curl -sS https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=up{job="inference-gateway"} | jq
     - rcli svc status inference-gateway --region us-west-2
   - If kv-cache eviction spike > 20% or error-rate > 2% / 5m window, activate cache-fallback policy (route to cold-read variant).
   - Coach performs live guidance and marks decision checkpoints in the bridge timeline.
3) Restore (30–180m)
   - If rollback is required, follow the rollback checklist in the runbook sections below.
   - For model-serving degradations, pin model to last-known-good revision and enable a lower-throughput fallback pool.
4) Remediate & communicate (3–72h)
   - Confirm root cause confidence >= 60% before claiming remediation on customer notices.
   - Begin RCA investigation and evidence collection.
5) Post-incident learning (3–14 days)
   - Produce postmortem with learning items, assigned owners, and remediation ETA. Coach approves the postmortem draft before it is shared with stakeholders.

Runbook templates (standardized modules):
- Title: "inference-gateway high-error-rate"
  - Pager signal: error_rate(inference-gateway) > 1.5% sustained for 5m OR p95 latency > 600ms for 5m
  - Immediate actions (ordered):
    1. Verify alert validity: query metrics and recent deploys.
    2. Toggle route-weight to standby pool: rcli routing weight inference-gateway production=0.25 standby=0.75
    3. If latency improves by >30% within 10m, continue staged rollback; else escalate.
  - Recovery criteria: sustained error_rate < 0.5% and p95 latency < 400ms for 15m
  - Evidence to capture: timeline entries, CLI outputs, deploy IDs, S3 artifact links to logs.

- Title: "kv-cache eviction storm"
  - Pager signal: mem_evictions_total{job="kv-cache"} increases by >300% vs baseline in 10m
  - Immediate actions:
    1. Enable cache-throttle: rcli cache throttle enable --percentage 75
    2. Roll forward eviction policy: set cache.max_ttl=30m (temporary)
    3. Notify CS/Support if tenant quotas likely exceeded.

On-call mentorship program (operational detail):
- New responders: two-week pairing with an experienced coach. Pairing schedule: 1 coach : 1 trainee for the first 10 on-call shifts (or 2 weeks).
- Check-ins: each coach completes a 30-minute debrief with trainee within 24 hours of each incident where the trainee was primary responder.
- Competency gates: to move from paired to solo on-call, the trainee must demonstrate:
  - Successful ownership of at least 3 incidents with coach sign-off.
  - Postmortem write-up participation on at least 1 incident.
  - Completion of the runbook lab (see Game Day section).
- Coaching playbook: coaches use the "teaching-first" checklist: ask the trainee to narrate their current hypothesis, suggest one corrective action, and confirm the trainee is able to run the command safely.

Game day curriculum (minimum quarterly for all responder engineers):
- Focus areas this year: KV cache eviction storms, prefix cache warm-up, and multi-region failover of inference-gateway.
- Format: 3-hour session; 45m tabletop, 60m live sim on staging, 30m debrief, 45m remediation lab.
- Scoring: time to containment, correctness of communication, and evidence completeness. Coaches grade and provide written feedback.

Customer & stakeholder communications (templates and rules):
- Principles: accurate, minimally technical for customers, transparent about impact and ETA, no speculative cause statements. All public-facing messages must be reviewed by Support/CSM if incident is SEV1 or impacts >5% of paying customers.

Status page template (short):
- Title: "Investigating: elevated request errors for inference API (US-West)"
- Body: "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting the inference API in US-West. Impact: some requests may return server errors or experience increased latency. Mitigation: traffic has been partially routed to standby hosts while we investigate. Next update: in 30 minutes or when new information is available."
- Internal note: include incident ID, affected regions, approximate customer count, and ownership.

Customer email snippet (when approved to send):
- Subject: "Update on inference API incident — partial mitigation in place"
- Body: "Hello — we want to let you know we observed elevated errors for the inference API in US-West between 11:05–12:20 PDT which affected approximately 8% of requests. We routed traffic to standby hosts and applied a model pin; the service returned to baseline at 12:20 PDT. We are running a follow-up RCA and will share a summary and remediation plan by <date>. If you observed specific customer-impacting behavior, please reply with request IDs or example timestamps so we can correlate logs."

Status page payload example (JSON for automation):
{
  "incident_id": "INC-20250612-4921",
  "severity": "SEV2",
  "services": ["inference-gateway"],
  "regions": ["us-west-2"],
  "impact": "partial",
  "summary": "Elevated 5xx errors for inference API; partial routing to standby hosts",
  "next_update_minutes": "30"
}

Postmortem & learning loop (format & timeline):
- Target: postmortem draft within 72 hours, final publish within 14 days.
- Required sections:
  1. TL;DR (15–25 words)
  2. Timeline (minute-by-minute for first 3 hours; then hourly until recovery)
  3. Impact (customers, SLOs, revenue risk)
  4. Root cause hypothesis and evidence (attach logs, graphs, deploy IDs)
  5. Immediate fixes and long-term remediations (owner + ETA)
  6. Learning items and improvements to runbooks/game day curriculum
- Coach sign-off: the coach must approve the evidence completeness section before the postmortem is accepted.

Operational metrics and SLO thresholds (what to measure):
- Availability SLO (hosted API): 99.95% monthly for production tier.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for inference-gateway (global).
- Error budget burn alert: if rolling 7-day availability drops below 99.9%, notify reliability council and schedule a mitigation review.
- On-call health metric: average time-to-acknowledge < 3m for SEV1/2, average time-to-contain < 30m for SEV2.

Appendix: quick commands & evidence checklist:
- Quick commands:
  - rcli incident create --title "<short title>" --sev SEV2 --bridge coach-first
  - rcli svc rollback inference-gateway --deploy-id 2025-06-12-0901
  - rcli routing shift inference-gateway --from production --to standby --pct 50
- Minimum evidence to attach to postmortem (artifact locations or links):
  - Prometheus queries and screenshots (preferred as .png),
  - Deploy manifest IDs and commit SHAs,
  - S3 log bundle link (s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-<id>/),
  - PagerDuty timeline export,
  - Bridge transcript (bridge link).

Related pages & ownership:
- Maintainer: engineering SRE guild (primary contact: eng-sre@redwood.com)
- Related: incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework (see related_pages).
